why: Both say: with a credible lead already forming and killers alive, stay unclaimed and back it with public-record facts; b6c99d08 also covers the tie-break case.
Both say: when a visit report or accuser puts you at a saved player's door, claim Healer and name whom you protected; cfecc64e adds corroboration and the rival-claimant case.
Both say: when asked to corroborate a claimant, confirm only the single fact you can verify; 119c8a46 adds when a full claim is justified.
Both say: night 1 with a blind kill, hold both conceals; c8cd609f gives the sound reason and avoids the carrier-choice error.
Both say: night 1 blind kill, spend a conceal on it; b177828b states the refund and trace mechanics correctly.
Both say: if the victim has already publicly claimed a role, do not conceal and keep the charges; 40785807 adds the tracker exception.
All say: conceal when the pack kills a claimed power or info role whose role or will would help the town; 1cd12b76 is correct on refund mechanics and avoids the carrier-choice error.
Both say: as the last wolf with conceals, make the kill and conceal it rather than pass; adcf1721 gives the target logic as well.
Both say: if the healer is likely guarding the obvious power-role target, pick another target; 78e2d08b states the conceal and visibility mechanics correctly.
All say: on the first usable-body night use a passive info body on a focal player rather than attack or waste a sigil; ebffd27d is the most complete.
Both say: with a usable attacking body and town info roles alive, attack the top info role and avoid the one the healer is covering; 5add9fdc is the more general.
Both say: on the day-2 first vote with no evidence and low heat, vote with the emerging majority and favour the concrete-friction target; 075b348c also covers the abstain majority.
Both say: with low heat and a strong majority forming, vote with it instead of dissenting or abstaining; 911e3c3f has no rules error.
Both say: on day 2 with a watch result, claim Sentinel and give the directional visitor list; 8f089210 adds inviting others to confirm.
Both say: with a visitor seen at the watched door, claim and name the visitor in plain wording; 6d7b8a5a adds repeating it under rebuttal.
Both say: night 2 after a tied vote, pick a victim the wolves are unlikely to hit; ed45616d adds the watcher-trace reasoning.
Both say: at three alive take the kill that leaves two; 69309443 also covers the 3-4 player vote math.
All say: on early nights with no hard lead hold fire and keep bullets; 379dfbbe also notes the Serial Killer immunity.
Both say: mid-to-late game after evil deaths with two bullets and no hard evidence, hold fire; 96246375 sets the evidence threshold.
Both say: mid-game with both killer factions active and no hard lead, stop holding and shoot the best-evidenced player; 580f91a9 has the clearer evidence rule.
Both say: late game, vote with the forming majority for the last unaccounted-for evil player found by elimination; 5585ec14 also covers the wolf case.
Both say: vote with the majority on the player contradicted by converging independent night reports; 2d0b01cd adds asking for corroboration if unpicked.
Both say: after a visible evil elimination with Town ahead, spend the Town pick now; 89062301 adds the mechanics that the pick is not a visit and counts after death.
Both say: if a hidden killer or wolf remains, delay the Town pick a night; 5daaf028 adds the target-risk exception.
